skill.name: mtls-configuration
skill.description: Configure mutual TLS for zero-trust service-to-service communication across Istio, Linkerd, cert-manager, and SPIFFE/SPIRE.
skill.summary: Guides teams through mTLS templates, certificate rotation, and troubleshooting for service mesh security.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were caused by Markdown code fences, service mesh configuration examples, resource links, and placeholder certificate paths in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, secret exfiltration intent, or hidden executable code. The skill is security-focused documentation, but users should review cluster commands before applying them.

remediation.issue: Placeholder certificate and key references may be mistaken for real secrets.
remediation.suggestion: State near the templates that certificate paths and encoded values are examples, and never include live private keys in shared manifests.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic command blocks can affect real clusters when copied directly.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to verify the current Kubernetes context and namespace before running rollout or inspection commands.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent mTLS configuration across service meshes and certificate tooling. This skill provides practical templates, checks, and troubleshooting steps for secure service-to-service communication.
actual_capabilities: Provides Istio PeerAuthentication and DestinationRule examples for strict and permissive mTLS.
Shows cert-manager resources for issuing short-lived workload certificates.
Includes SPIFFE/SPIRE server and agent configuration examples.
Covers Linkerd mTLS verification and exception patterns.
Lists certificate rotation and handshake debugging checks.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to local namespaces, trust domains, and certificate authorities.
The skill does not validate a live cluster or certificate chain by itself.
It does not replace service mesh vendor documentation or compliance review.
Command examples should be reviewed before use on production clusters.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Namespace to Strict mTLS
use_cases.description: Plan a safe move from permissive mode to strict service-to-service authentication.

use_cases.title: Design Certificate Rotation
use_cases.description: Create a short-lived certificate workflow with cert-manager and operational checks.

use_cases.title: Debug Mesh Handshake Failures
use_cases.description: Use mesh status, identity, and log checks to isolate mTLS failures.

prompt_templates.title: Enable Namespace mTLS
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to enable strict mTLS for one Kubernetes namespace using Istio. Include the migration order and checks before enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Service Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Istio mTLS plan for a payments service that currently talks to legacy services. Include permissive migration, DestinationRules, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build Certificate Rotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a certificate rotation workflow for Istio workloads using cert-manager. Include renewal timing, monitoring signals, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Mesh Identity Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Istio, Linkerd, and SPIFFE/SPIRE for multi-cluster zero-trust communication. Recommend one approach for regulated workloads and explain tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Request: Enable strict mTLS for a namespace.
output_examples.output: A staged migration checklist with permissive mode, policy review, strict enforcement, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Request: Debug a failed handshake between two services.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic sequence covering service identity, destination policy, certificate status, proxy logs, and namespace scope.

output_examples.input: Request: Plan certificate rotation for workloads.
output_examples.output: A rotation plan with short certificate lifetimes, renewal windows, monitoring signals, and rollback considerations.

best_practices: Start migrations in permissive mode, then enforce strict mTLS after validation.
Use short-lived workload certificates and monitor expiry before outages occur.
Keep trust domains, namespaces, and service identities explicit in every template.
anti_patterns: Disabling mTLS on production ports to bypass a failing deployment.
Embedding real private keys or CA material in shared configuration examples.
Applying mesh-wide strict policies before legacy service dependencies are mapped.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production certificates?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration patterns and guidance. Use approved tooling to generate and store certificates.

faq.question: Which service meshes are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Istio, Linkerd, SPIFFE/SPIRE, and cert-manager examples for Kubernetes environments.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it handle real private keys?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholders and file paths. Do not paste real private keys into prompts or shared files.

faq.question: Is it limited to Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Most examples assume Kubernetes and a service mesh. The principles can inform other mTLS deployments.

faq.question: Should commands be run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review the current cluster context, namespace, and permissions before running any operational command.
